Fires on the modifier/first element of a multi-word compound name — especially food compounds ("banana" bread, "Pumpkin" Spice, "Blue-berry" Cake) and appositive "the" in "Jeremiah the prophet" — i.e. a noun-modifier slot anticipating a following head noun; it is strongly suppressed by the linking preposition "of" in genitive noun-of-noun phrases (hardening **of** Pharaoh's heart, king **of** Egypt) and by dessert-texture words like "crumble/crisp".
